classification.difficultyReason: Split each absolute value at zero, sketch its two linear branches and verify selected values, then reproduce each graph by scaling the y-coordinates of y=|x|. The methods are supplied, but students must link piecewise rules, numerical tables and vertical dilations and check their agreement.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch each function using cases. Check the graph with a table of values.

inlines.text: . Draw both branches through the origin. The table confirms the points.

spec.description: V graph with dashed guides through (-1,2) and (1,2).

inlines.text: . Draw both branches through the origin. The table confirms the points.

spec.description: V graph with guides through (-2,1) and (2,1).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Now sketch each function using a suitable vertical dilation of $y=|x|$, and check that you get the same graph.

answer.short: i. $y=2|x|$, a vertical stretch by factor 2. ii. $y=\frac12|x|$, a vertical stretch by factor $\frac12$. Both agree with part a.
answer.worked: For i, multiply every y-coordinate of $y=|x|$ by 2. The points $(-1,1)$ and $(1,1)$ become $(-1,2)$ and $(1,2)$. For ii, multiply every y-coordinate by $\frac12$. The points $(-2,2)$ and $(2,2)$ become $(-2,1)$ and $(2,1)$. Both vertices stay at $(0,0)$, giving the same respective graphs as in part a.

spec.description: Dilation result, matching the case sketch in part a i.
Dilation result, matching the case sketch in part a ii.
